clue.text: Composer's catalogue with unknown entry

definitions.note: the definition stands for 'the composer is', the 's linking it to the wordplay

indicators.note: the unknown is given entry into the catalogue, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a catalogue is a list
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A musician's list of works includes one mysterious item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entry' puts Z (an algebraic unknown) inside LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and pianist.

clue.text: Mysterious thing about deep depression in Scotland

definitions.text: Mysterious thing about deep depression in Scotland

parts.words: Mysterious thing about deep depression in Scotland
parts.note: a deep depression in Scotland is a loch, here a famous deep lake near Inverness; the mysterious thing is the creature said to live in it

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster describes something strange about a low-pressure system over Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep depression' reads like weather, but it is a long, deep Highland lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary creature reputedly seen in a Highland lake is a famous unexplained mystery.

clue.text: Suspended cast

definitions.meaning: hung up, as a hammock or a sling
thrown, as in tossing something carelessly

explanation.definitionFit: Both are senses of the past tense of a verb meaning to hang or to fling.

clue.text: Object about computer studies being taxing

indicators.note: the object goes round the computer studies, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: an object is a thing
IT, information technology, is the school subject of computer studies

explanation.surface: Someone protests that computer studies are being taxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taxing' looks like the adjective 'demanding' but is a noun for levying a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithing is paying or levying a tenth of produce or income, a form of taxation.

clue.text: Doing mathematics at university that's abstract

parts.note: doing sums is summing
UP means in residence at university, as in going up to Oxford

explanation.surface: Studying maths at college is too theoretical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstract' looks like the adjective but is the noun for a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a brief summary, which is what a judge's closing review gives.

clue.text: Unhesitatingly like one to be fired

definitions.meaning: 'like a ...' means without hesitation, so the answer completes the phrase
a bullet or round fired from a gun

explanation.definitionFit: A discharge from a gun is a shot, and 'like a shot' is an idiom for instantly.

clue.text: Economic type is into painter and painting

parts.note: Claude Monet, the French Impressionist

indicators.note: is goes into painting, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: An economist is described as keen on an Impressionist and his canvases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' reads like 'keen on' in the surface, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A monetarist is an economist who holds that controlling the money supply governs the economy.

clue.text: Charge one maiden minimal cost per item

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
a penny, abbreviated P, is the smallest cost
each means per item

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper charges one young woman the least possible price for every item.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to formally accuse an official of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Elderly relative's outbreak of rage over insult

definitions.note: stands for 'the elderly relative is', the 's linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits over the second
an outbreak breaks the word rage apart so its letters are scattered

parts.note: to taunt is to insult

explanation.surface: An old aunt flies into a temper at being insulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outbreak of' makes GREA from RAGE; 'over' puts it above TAUNT in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's aunt is a relative of an older generation.

clue.text: Measure of work that can be done from elevated position

definitions.text: Measure of work that can be done from elevated position

parts.words: Measure of work that can be done from elevated position
parts.note: a physics term for the stored capacity of a raised object to do work, phrased as if about a job done from a height

explanation.surface: A description of how much one can achieve from a high post.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, a raised mass stores energy by virtue of its height, available to do work as it falls.

clue.text: Prepare to launch television programme

definitions.meaning: counting the seconds down before a rocket lifts off
a long-running British TV quiz of words and numbers

explanation.walkthrough: The British TV show is a daytime words-and-numbers game.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are a reverse count of numbers, one before a rocket launch, one a quiz show title.

clue.text: English opener in place at the crease

indicators.note: the opener is put in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
taken as written

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A batsman from England opens the innings at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture (an opening batsman at the crease) misleads; the crease here is a fold in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a pressed fold in fabric, a kind of crease.

clue.text: Gill is endlessly kissing

indicators.note: without its ends, so the first and last letters of the synonym are dropped

parts.note: snogging is British slang for kissing passionately

explanation.surface: A girl named Gill is always kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOGGING (British slang for kissing) loses its first and last letters. Gill looks like a name but is a liquid measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A noggin is a small drink measure, a quarter of a pint, as is a gill.

clue.text: Impose restrictions on model train set

indicators.note: a model is a remade version, so the letters are rebuilt into a new form

explanation.surface: A hobbyist's toy railway is subject to new rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' sits naturally beside 'train set' but signals rearranging its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to confine or restrict, as in straitened circumstances.

clue.text: New family member introduces female engineer

indicators.note: the family member takes the female into itself, putting it inside

parts.note: a stepson joins a family by remarriage
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A stepchild brings a woman engineer into the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' points to George Stephenson, the 19th-century railway pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stephenson was the railway engineer who built the Rocket locomotive.

clue.text: Expression of joy after second massacre

indicators.note: the expression of joy comes after the second, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: laughter expresses joy

explanation.surface: A gleeful cry follows shortly after a bloodbath.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter is the brutal killing of many, a massacre.

clue.text: Sport a university has to obstruct

parts.note: taken as written
to cross someone is to thwart or obstruct them

explanation.surface: A college must block a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocross is motor racing round a rough grass or dirt course.

clue.text: Not before time, I found a beautiful woman

indicators.note: the letter I comes not before but after time, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

explanation.surface: Arriving none too soon, someone meets a lovely woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not before' reads as 'none too soon' but puts I after HOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is a beautiful maiden of the Islamic paradise, hence any lovely young woman.

clue.text: Saw doctor with grossly inflated middle

indicators.note: the inflated piece is placed in the middle of the doctor

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a military doctor
OTT, over the top, means excessive or overblown

explanation.surface: A doctor with a swollen belly saw something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb or tool but is a noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying, a maxim or adage.

clue.text: Camping area in Africa to stretch further?

definitions.meaning: in South Africa, a place where wagon teams were unharnessed to rest or camp
a playful reading as ..., to span or reach further out

explanation.definitionFit: Outspan is a South African word for unyoking draught animals, and the spot used for it, punned on as spanning outward.

clue.text: Later than delivery of mail to part of Africa

parts.note: post is mail
Natal is a province region of South Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal

explanation.surface: A letter turns up late in a region of southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests the post, but it means childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Postnatal describes the period following childbirth.

clue.text: Apprehensive, but showing gumption round middle of interview

indicators.note: the gumption goes round the middle piece, enclosing it

parts.note: nous is common sense or gumption

indicators.note: the central letters of the word interview are taken

explanation.surface: A job candidate is anxious yet shows some sense midway through the interview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the central three letters of the nine-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous means anxious or fearful, which is being apprehensive.

clue.text: Subtle details of links with French resort

indicators.note: the links are joined with the resort, here following it in the answer

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
ties are links or bonds

explanation.surface: Fine points about golf links near a Riviera town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links' suggests golf but means ties.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are fine distinctions or small points of detail.

clue.text: It's cooler in the capital without article on

indicators.note: the capital loses the article, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France
A is the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that it is chillier in the French capital without one item on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' looks like a temperature but is slang for a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooler is slang for a jail, a place of confinement.

clue.text: Desert -— an offence of the highest order

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Abandoning someone is described as a top-grade wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a verb but is the noun for the Egyptian peninsula's desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the desert peninsula of Egypt, where Moses received the commandments.

clue.text: Some Indian tea, one for the pot

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A portion of Indian tea is a spoonful for the teapot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pot' suggests a teapot, but it is the poker kitty.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker an ante is a stake each player puts in the kitty before the deal.

clue.text: Men about to enter crack cavalry unit

indicators.note: the men go into the crack, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: crack means first-rate or top

indicators.note: about means the word for men is turned round

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are enlisted men

explanation.surface: Soldiers are poised to join an elite mounted regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' is the adjective for first-rate, as in crack troops, not a split.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a cavalry subunit, like a company of infantry.

clue.text: Order new rounds of drink

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A customer at the bar asks for fresh rounds of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as asking the barman but rearranges NEW ROUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset.

clue.text: Re-echo on a screen needs to be fixed

indicators.note: something needing fixing is broken, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A TV screen showing an echo needs repairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs to be fixed' rearranges ON A SCREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonance is sound prolonged by reverberation, an echoing.

clue.text: Reflecting how shoes should be, but not trousers

definitions.text: Reflecting how shoes should be, but not trousers

parts.words: Reflecting how shoes should be, but not trousers
parts.note: polished footwear should gleam, but worn trouser seats that gleam are a sign of age

explanation.surface: A grooming tip: polish shoes, but trousers should never gleam.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy and light-reflecting describes well-polished shoes, while threadbare trousers go glossy at the seat.
